headline: Opposition to data centers has spread to Europe and South Korea and has stalled about $42 billion of European projects, research firm STL Partners says.
score_reason: Pool 6 kept: a broad shift with numbers, relayed one day after the original report.
importance_line: Residents near planned sites and investors in European data centers are affected, but the figures come from one research firm via a relay and not all delays are cancellations.
summary: BigGo Finance reports, relaying a CNBC story of 3 Oct 2026, that public opposition has delayed or cancelled about $42 billion of data center investment in Europe, according to research firm STL Partners, and that local resistance is also growing in South Korea. The European Data Center Monitor counts more than 70 European projects rejected or restricted between January and April, more than in all of 2025, as places such as Ireland, Scotland and Denmark limit new sites over power demand.
notes: Credit to CNBC (first reporter, per the relay); CNBC original not opened. Score not lowered because the CNBC report is one day old.
